teams.heading: Fiji concede an average of 29.6 points across their last 11 matches
teams.body: Fiji have conceded 326 points in total across their last 11 games. This defensive record averages out to 29.6 points conceded per match over that 11-game span. At the other end of the pitch, the team scored 315 points over the same 11-game period, maintaining an average of 28.6 points per fixture. The brightest point of this 11-match sequence remains the home test in September 2025, where they achieved their biggest victory of the window by beating Canada 63-10 in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick hands five stars first England deals in major squad shake-up
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has finalised his 25-man list of enhanced Elite Player Squad contracts, rewarding form by handing first-time deals to Seb Atkinson, Alex Coles, Asher Opoku-Fordjour, Guy Pepper and Jack van Poortvliet. The £150,000 agreements grant Borthwick control over medical and conditioning matters for the upcoming season. However, there is no space for Ben Curry or Ollie Lawrence, while Elliot Daly also misses out. The reshuffle prioritises recent Nations Championship regulars, with Atkinson and van Poortvliet now central to England’s new-look playmaking axis.

lead.why: The finalisation of senior central contracts and the high-profile omissions of established internationals represent the most significant squad news for the upcoming November tests.

teams.heading: Vlok Cilliers joins the Bulls following shock France national team departure
teams.body: Long-serving kicking coach Vlok Cilliers has returned to the Bulls after ending his seven-year tenure with the French national team. His exit, confirmed by the French Rugby Federation, was part of a broader shake-up by head coach Fabien Galthié aimed at refreshing the squad for the upcoming World Cup cycle. Cilliers, credited with refining Thomas Ramos’s goal-kicking, noted that after his time in France, the opportunity to reunite with Johan Ackermann in Pretoria proved impossible to resist.

teams.heading: Former Wallabies and Ireland international Brian Smith dies aged 59
teams.body: The rugby world is mourning the loss of former Ireland and Wallabies international Brian Smith, who has died at the age of 59. A versatile half-back, Smith earned 9 caps for Ireland after beginning his international career with 6 appearances for Australia. Following his playing days, he enjoyed a distinguished coaching career, including a stint as England’s assistant coach and director of rugby at London Irish. He is remembered by those he mentored as a “Great bloke, father and coach”.

lead.why: The passing of a dual-international who represented Ireland is the most significant news item in today's rugby coverage.

teams.heading: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada receives two-match ban from World Rugby
teams.body: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has been issued a two-match suspension by World Rugby. The ban follows critical comments regarding match official performance after the recent meeting with New Zealand. Under the newly implemented Match Official Abuse Sanctioning Process, this suspension excludes Quesada from all match-day proceedings for Italy's upcoming meeting with South Africa. The coach retains the right to appeal this decision to a full judicial committee.

lead.why: The head coach's suspension under the new disciplinary process is a significant development for the team's management.

teams.heading: Alun Wyn Jones set to join Ospreys board amid regional uncertainty
teams.body: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones is set to join the Ospreys as a director next week. The 40-year-old’s return arrives at a turbulent time as the club contests the Welsh Rugby Union’s plan to reduce the number of professional men’s sides in Wales to three. The Ospreys, who maintain that a four-team model is the correct path for the game, have recently undergone significant personnel changes, including a busy recruitment drive following the departure of senior players.

teams.heading: Tomás Albornoz serves four-match suspension for intimidating referee Angus Gardner
teams.body: Fly-half Tomás Albornoz remains sidelined as he serves a four-match suspension following his conduct after the defeat to England. The disciplinary committee found that Albornoz acted in an intimidatory manner toward referee Angus Gardner, noting that the player made contact with the official and required restraint by his teammates. Having accepted the misconduct allegations, the fly-half is currently ineligible for selection while he completes the sanction, which was handed down following the conclusion of the England match.

lead.why: The disciplinary status of a key squad member remains the most significant ongoing narrative following the recent England Test.

teams.heading: Australia dominates Japan as Taniela Tupou inspires Townsville second-half romp
teams.body: Australia secured three consecutive Test victories for the first time since 2024, overwhelming Japan 56-17 in Townsville on Saturday. Despite a tight first half, the Wallabies surged in the second period, scoring 35 unanswered points to dismantle the Brave Blossoms. Taniela Tupou crossed for two tries, while debutant prop Massimo De Lutiis also scored in a dominant display. Coach Les Kiss stated, “This Saturday in Townsville gives us an opportunity to grow and strengthen our game on home soil.”

lead.why: It is the primary result of the weekend, marking Australia's first three-match winning streak since 2024.

teams.heading: Japan suffer heavy 56-17 defeat to dominant Australia in Townsville
teams.body: Japan’s Nations Championship campaign faced a setback on Saturday as they fell to a 56-17 defeat against Australia. After a competitive opening period that saw Harry Hockings and Naoto Saitō cross for tries to keep the score tight, the Brave Blossoms were eventually overwhelmed by a ruthless Australian pack. Australia secured a 35-0 second-half margin, with Japan's discipline faltering late as Harada received a yellow card. This result follows a tighter 35-32 loss in the previous round.

teams.heading: Caleb Clarke ruled out of All Blacks’ tour after shoulder injury
teams.body: The All Blacks’ backline depth has been tested further with confirmation that winger Caleb Clarke will fly home after rupturing a tendon in his shoulder during Tuesday’s win over the Sharks. Clarke is the second backline casualty of the tour, following centre Billy Proctor’s earlier exit. Head coach Dave Rennie has stated that no immediate replacement will be called up to the squad, though he noted that performances in Saturday's fixture against the Bulls could still influence final Test selection.

lead.why: The loss of Caleb Clarke to a serious shoulder injury is a significant, immediate personnel blow to the touring squad.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus confirms returning Springbok duo following Bulls franchise tour duty
teams.body: Head coach Rassie Erasmus is set to bolster his squad on Sunday as hooker Johan Grobbelaar and utility forward Elrigh Louw rejoin the national setup. The pair were released to represent the Vodacom Bulls during their tour clash against the All Blacks. Following the completion of a rotated training camp, Erasmus expressed confidence in the group’s readiness for next Saturday’s opening test at Ellis Park, noting, “We are pleased that the players are well recovered and ready to give everything.”
